# 2026-11-04 中文 NBA 每日简报

（北京时间 2026-11-04 17:48 编制。联盟因美国选举日休赛一天，今日无比赛；以下为最近一轮赛果与最新伤病动态，共三条。）

## 1. 比赛结果：最近一轮 15 场，鹈鹕送灰熊首败、火箭登顶西部
- 鹈鹕 135-134 灰熊（加时）：灰熊冲击队史首次 7-0 开局未果，泰·杰罗姆砍下 40 分，锡安·威廉森 25 分 11 篮板。
- 火箭 109-93 凯尔特人：火箭 7 胜 1 负，反超灰熊升至西部第一；申京 26 分 7 篮板 10 助攻。
- 湖人 138-117 热火：东契奇 42 分 13 助攻 7 篮板，连续第 5 场拿到 35+5+5+5 记三分。
- 雷霆 117-112 骑士：亚历山大 43 分 8 助攻，终场前 33 秒命中制胜三分。
- 来源：NBA.com《Starting 5: Monday's packed 15-game slate ahead of Election Day》，发布时间 2026-11-03 15:44（美东时间，即北京时间 11-04 04:44）。链接：https://www.nba.com/news/starting-5-november-3-2026
- 比分核对：虎扑 NBA 比赛中心 2026-11-03 赛果页（检索于北京时间 2026-11-04 17:49）。链接：https://nba.hupu.com/games/2026-11-03
- 备注：该轮为美东 11 月 2 日（周一）的 15 场比赛，北京时间 11 月 3 日结束；因选举日休赛，北京时间 11 月 4 日无比赛，下一轮在北京时间 11 月 5 日。

## 2. 伤病：步行者 11 人伤停，仅 6 人应战老鹰
- 步行者对老鹰一战有 11 名球员因伤或轮休缺阵（约占球队薪资 93%），只能派出 6 人轮换，最终 104-108 落败。
- 缺阵球员：哈利伯顿（腿筋）、西亚卡姆（轮休）、内姆哈德（颈部）、内史密斯（腿筋）、托平（腰椎扭伤）、祖巴茨（脚踝）、麦康奈尔（腿筋）、约翰尼·弗尔菲（膝）、小拉里·南斯（生病）、本·谢泼德（膝）；凯利·乌布雷赛前因膝部挫伤临时退出。
- 主帅卡莱尔赛前称这是“各种情况同时发生的完美风暴”，并表示“必须聪明应对”。
- 来源：NBA.com 转载美联社《5 starters, 1 sub: Pacers down to 6 players vs. Hawks》，发布时间 2026-11-03 04:18（美东时间，即北京时间 11-03 17:18）。链接：https://www.nba.com/news/5-starters-1-sub-pacers-down-to-6-players-for-game-against-atlanta-because-of-injuries-rest

## 3. 伤病：莱昂纳德完成左膝消肿治疗，启动“回归比赛”流程
- 猛龙官方宣布，莱昂纳德“已成功完成针对左膝肿胀的治疗”，开始“回归比赛（return to play）”流程。
- 他将至少再缺席 3 场，球队一周后更新进展；按此推算，最早可能在 11 月 11 日对阵凯尔特人时复出。
- 莱昂纳德本季前两场场均 19.5 分 7.5 篮板，缺阵期间猛龙 2 胜 3 负。
- 来源：NBA.com 转载美联社《Raptors say Leonard has started 'return to play' process》，发布时间 2026-11-04 01:17（美东时间，即北京时间 11-04 14:17）。链接：https://www.nba.com/news/kawhi-leonards-knee-swelling-has-been-treated-and-hell-start-return-to-play-process-raptors-say

5 starters, 1 sub: Pacers down to 6 players for game against Atlanta because of injuries, rest
The Pacers had 11 players out with injuries for Monday's game against the Hawks, leaving Indiana six players to choose from.
The Associated Press
November 3, 2026 4:18 AM
Jarace Walker was one of only six available Pacers to play in Monday’s loss to the Hawks.
Indiana had a starting five on Monday night. And a reserve.
That was it.
The Pacers had 11 players – representing about 93% of their payroll – out with injuries for their game against the Atlanta Hawks. That left Indiana six players to choose from, putting the Pacers in a precarious position.
“It’s kind of a perfect storm of things happening at once,” coach Rick Carlisle said in his news conference before the game in Indianapolis. “It’s unlucky. But we have to be smart here.”
Carlisle said that about 90 minutes before game time, thinking at that point he’d have seven players. Things actually got worse not long afterward, when Kelly Oubre Jr. was a late scratch because of a bruised knee.
With that, Indiana was down to six – making Monday the first time since 2004 that the Pacers would use so few players in a game.
The previous low for players used
in a game so far this season was eight, by Philadelphia on Oct. 25. There have been seven other instances of teams using six players over the last 15 seasons – almost all of those in meaningless contests toward the end of a season.
The last time a team used only six players in a game during the first few weeks of a season was on Nov. 24, 2009, when Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors – with some players getting cramps massaged out of their legs during timeouts – somehow beat the Dallas Mavericks 111-103.
Along with Oubre, the rundown of those missing: Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring), Pascal Siakam (rest), Johnny Furphy (knee), T.J. McConnell (hamstring), Larry Nance Jr. (illness), Andrew Nembhard (cervical), Aaron Nesmith (hamstring), Ben Sheppard (knee), Obi Toppin (lumbar sprain) and Ivica Zubac (ankle).
Some players are out for weeks; some just couldn’t go Monday, with Indiana on the second night of a back-to-back. “Injury management,” Carlisle said.
That left the Pacers with one player
making more than $3 million this season – Jarace Walker. Add it all up, and Indiana had about $193 million in salary sitting and about $15 million in salary playing.
The rest of Indiana’s available players included Jay Huff, Quenton Jackson and three players on two-way deals: Braden Smith, Jalen Slawson and Kobe Brown. Smith got the first start of his NBA career, with Walker, Slawson, Huff and Jackson joining him in the starting lineup. Brown came off the bench.
“There’s going to be some real opportunity,” Carlisle said.
Indiana next plays on Wednesday at Memphis. The Pacers don’t play Tuesday – the entire league has the day off for Election Day – and are off Thursday and Friday as well.

Kawhi Leonard's knee swelling has been treated and he’ll start ‘return to play’ process, Raptors say
Kawhi Leonard, who hasn’t played due to a swollen knee, has started the ‘return to play’ process, the Toronto Raptors say.
Associated Press
November 4, 2026 1:17 AM
Kawhi Leonard, who hasn’t played due to a swollen knee, has started the ‘return to play’ process, the Toronto Raptors say.
TORONTO (AP) —
Kawhi Leonard is getting closer to rejoining the Toronto Raptors’ lineup.
The Raptors announced Tuesday that Leonard “has successfully completed treatment to address left knee swelling,” the first step in the process to get him back on the court again.
Leonard played in Toronto’s first two games of the season, averaging 19.5 points and 7.5 rebounds. The Raptors have been without him since, going 2-3 in five contests.
He’ll miss at least three more games while going through what the team called “the return to play” process in Toronto. Leonard’s progress will be updated in a week, Raptors said, meaning the earliest he could play again would be Nov. 11 against Boston.
Leonard is a two-time NBA Finals MVP, including when he led the Raptors to their lone title in 2019. After getting traded back to Toronto this summer, he agreed to a
$115 million extension
that, at his option, would run through the 2028-29 season.

Starting 5: Monday's packed 15-game slate ahead of Election Day
Looking back at Monday's 15-game slate as the NBA pauses to encourage voting on Election Day.
NBA.com Staff
November 3, 2026 3:44 PM
NBA Nightly Recap
SGA scores season-high 43, Pelicans snap Grizzlies winning streak, Luka stuffs stat sheet, and more from Monday's 15-game slate.
A floater’s roll,
sealed with a kiss.
And a historic heater
that you don’t wanna miss.
5 STORIES IN TODAY’S EDITION 🏀
Monday’s Best:
OT thriller in Memphis, Houston takes West lead, Luka breaks more records
More West Wins:
SGA hangs 43, Steph erupts again, Spurs extend streak, Blazers stay balling
East Heat:
Sixers stars shine, Cade powers Pistons, Knicks respond in 4th quarter
Roundup:
Dybantsa delivers, LaMelo lifts Wolves, NAW pops off, Raptors rally, Kings win
Election Day Is Here:
Make your voice heard as the NBA pauses play to encourage voting
BUT FIRST … ⏰
U.S. Election Day:
The NBA pauses play today to encourage civic participation as Americans head to the polls for the 2026 midterms. Visit the
NBA’s Election Day Hub
for additional voting resources, and see Section 5 for more on the league’s efforts.
Play resumes Wednesday
with 14 games, headlined by an ESPN doubleheader: 76ers-Pistons (
7 ET
), Mavericks-Spurs (
9:30 ET
).
Russ To The Rafters:
The Thunder announced they will
retire Russell Westbrook’s No. 0 on Feb. 7
against the defending champion Knicks, honoring the 2016-17 Kia MVP after 11 seasons with OKC.
1. MONDAY’S BEST: PELS EDGE GRIZZ IN OT, ROCKETS RISE, LUKA DAZZLES
Justin Ford/NBAE via Getty Images
The NBA’s last unbeaten team
went down Monday night. But it took more than 48 minutes to knock them off.
Pelicans 135, Grizzlies 134 (OT):
With Memphis seeking its first 7-0 start in franchise history, Ty Jerome went off, dropping
40 points on 14-for-22 shooting
, including a personal 9-0 closing run in the final 1:43 to force extra basketball.
But Zion Williamson
(25 pts, 11 reb, 4 ast) and the Pels gutted out a win in a back-and-forth overtime, surviving Jerome’s heroics to hand Memphis its first loss (6-1). |
Recap
Late Drama:
Jerome (5 reb, 5 ast, 5 3s) scored 8 points in OT, including a go-ahead and-1 with 18 seconds left, but Jeremiah Fears retook the lead for NOLA with a pair of late free throws, and the Pels stood tall on the
game’s final possession
“The ability to find a way
down the stretch … that’s what I’m most proud of,” said Pelicans coach Jamahl Mosley postgame. “The resiliency, the toughness, the grit that these guys showed – that’s what it’s gotta look like.”
Pels Flock:
Zion led all players with 9 points in the extra frame, while Karlo Matković (career-high 25 pts) and Derik Queen (20 pts, 7 reb, 5 ast) each finished with 20+
Ode To Jerome:
Jerome recorded just one 30-point game in his first seven NBA seasons. He’s already done it three times in six games this year
Logan Riely/NBAE via Getty Images
As Memphis went down
for the first time, the Rockets kept rising.
Rockets 109, Celtics 93:
Houston entered the night as the only team with eight players averaging double figures and leaned on that balance to hand Boston its first loss since its season opener, with eight Rockets scoring 8+ points.
Alperen Sengun
(26 pts, 7 reb, 10 ast) led the way, while Marcus Smart starred defensively against his former team, helping the Rockets hold the C’s under 100 points for the first time this season. |
Recap
New No. 1:
With the win, Houston (7-1) leapfrogged Memphis for 1st place in the West, with both teams tied for the NBA’s best plus-minus (+12.9)
As the Rockets ascended,
Luka Dončić continued to reach new heights.
Lakers 138, Heat 117:
Less than 24 hours after posting an unprecedented stat line, Luka rewrote more records, racking up
42 points, 13 dimes, 7 boards and 6 treys
as the Lakers sprinted past Giannis Antetokounmpo (30 pts, 12 reb, 7 ast) and Miami for their second win in two nights. |
Recap
Historic Heater:
It’s Dončić’s fifth straight game with 35+ pts, 5+ reb, 5+ ast and 5+ 3s, matching Damian Lillard (Jan. 2020) for the longest such streak in NBA history
Absurd Averages:
Over those five games, Luka is averaging a ridiculous 43.4 pts, 8.6 ast, 8.4 reb and 6.8 3s per game, capped by 40-pieces on back-to-back nights
Generational Problem:
To top it off? Monday marked his 19th career game with 40+ points, 10+ dimes and 5+ triples, passing James Harden (18) for the most all-time
2. MORE WEST WINS: SGA & STEPH TAKE OVER, SPURS & BLAZERS STAY HOT
Two more former scoring champions
took over Monday with timely outbursts.
Thunder 117, Cavaliers 112:
In a game that featured an NBA season-high 23 lead changes, the reigning Kia Clutch Player of the Year – and back-to-back Kia MVP – delivered the decisive swing, as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (43 pts, 8 ast) buried a
tiebreaking 3 with 33 ticks left
to lift OKC over Cleveland. |
Recap
Taking Charge:
SGA scored 26 points in the 2nd half, 13 in each quarter, while matching his career-high with 35 FGA to help snap the shorthanded Thunder’s two-game skid
“There’s certain nights,
when you have a player like that, when you just kind of unleash them,” said Thunder coach Mark Daigneault of SGA postgame. “And he had it going.”
Warriors 116, Suns 113:
Back from a one-game absence, Steph Curry picked up right where he left off (
34 pts, 6 reb, 7 ast
), erupting for an 18-point 3rd quarter as Golden State rallied past Devin Booker (26 pts, 5 ast) and Phoenix for its fifth straight dub. |
Recap
3rd-Quarter Blitz:
With the Warriors down six at the half, Curry turned up, going 4-for-5 from deep to spark a 42-point barrage from Golden State, which held off a late Phoenix push to move to 5-3
30 For 30:
Curry has dropped 30+ points in three straight games (44, 31, 34), climbing to 2nd in the NBA in scoring (30 ppg)
More Dubs:
After a monster Sunday, Yaxel Lendeborg tallied 16 points and 5 dimes, while Brandin Podziemski scored 20
Also winners
of five straight? The reigning West champs.
Spurs 119, Jazz 97:
Seven Spurs reached double figures, powered by their young backcourt tandem of Dylan Harper (17 pts, 7 reb, 8 ast) and Stephon Castle (16 pts, 4 ast), as San Antonio rolled past Utah to move to 5-2 after an 0-2 start. |
Recap
Wemby’s Way:
Victor Wembanyama, the
Western Conference Player of the Week
for Week 2, added 12 points, 11 boards, 5 dimes and 3 blocks in the win
Blazers 118, Nuggets 110:
Jamal Murray (35 pts, 6 ast) and Nikola Jokić (26 pts, 9 reb, 8 ast, 4 stl) put on a show in Mile High, but the Blazers came out on top, climbing out of a 14-point 1st-half hole to edge Denver. |
Recap
Blazing Hot:
Deni Avdija (28 pts, 5 ast) and Damian Lillard (20 pts, 6 ast) powered Portland’s attack, which ranks 4th in scoring (120.2 ppg)
Two-Way Trouble:
Donovan Clingan (17 pts, 18 reb, 4 blk) and Jrue Holiday (17 pts, 10 ast) delivered on both ends, helping hold Denver to 38.5% from the field after halftime
On The Up:
Portland is now 5-1, sitting just a game back of Houston for 1st place in the West
3. EAST HEAT: SIXERS SHINE, PISTONS ROLL, KNICKS RESPOND
76ers 126, Bulls 107:
Tyrese Maxey (26 pts, 11 ast), Jaylen Brown (25 pts, 11 reb) and VJ Edgecombe (21 pts) all scored 20+, with Maxey dropping 15 in the 4th as the Sixers pulled past Chicago for their fourth straight win, improving to an East-best 7-1. |
Recap
Philly Five:
LeBron James (7 reb, 9 ast) and Joel Embiid (8 reb) added 15 points apiece as the Sixers’ starting five
combined for 102
Ty Time:
Maxey, who ranks 3rd in the NBA in scoring (29.1 ppg), leads the league with 88 4th-quarter points – 26 more than the next closest player (Ty Jerome: 62)
Rookie Shine:
No. 4 overall pick Caleb Wilson paced Chicago with a big all-around night (24 pts, 7 reb, 4 ast, 4 stl)
Pistons 124, Hornets 91:
Detroit’s top-rated defense held Charlotte to just 38.1% from the field, while Cade Cunningham took over on both ends (
33 pts, 5 reb, 7 ast, 5 stl
) as the Pistons secured their third straight dub to move to 6-1. |
Recap
DBo From Deep:
Duncan Robinson added 24 points on 6-for-9 shooting from 3. He now has four games with 5+ triples this season, trailing only Luka (6)
Knicks 103, Nets 90:
Down four after three quarters, the Knicks opened the 4th on a 25-5 run to take control, racing past the rival Nets to earn a timely win. Landry Shamet led the way with 22 points on four 3s, while Karl-Anthony Towns added a double-double (11 pts, 16 reb). |
Recap
4. ROUNDUP: DYBANTSA, NAW & BALL SHOW OUT, RAPTORS & KINGS WIN
Gary Bassing + Luther Schlaifer/NBAE via Getty Images
Wizards 103, Magic 94:
The high-flying connection between AJ Dybantsa (21 pts, 5 reb) and Trae Young
continues to grow
, while Anthony Davis continues to eat (27 pts, 9 reb, 4 stl) as the Wiz earned their second straight win to move to 4-3. |
Recap
New Era, Strong Start:
Young tallied 15 points and 9 dimes, helping Washington move above .500 through seven games for the first time in five years
Hawks 108, Pacers 104:
A six-man Pacers rotation gave the Hawks everything they could handle, but there was no cooling down Nickeil Alexander-Walker, who drilled nine 3s en route to a game-high 34 points as Atlanta held off Indy. |
Recap
Wolves 112, Bucks 100:
LaMelo Ball (34 pts, 6 3s) netted
24 points in the 1st half
on five treys, before Minnesota used a 16-5 run to take control early in the 4th, riding another strong defensive effort for its fifth win in eight games. |
Recap
Minny Clamps:
The Wolves, who rank 2nd in defensive rating (104.6), have held their opponents to 106 points or fewer in all five of their wins
Raptors 125, Clippers 118:
Down as many as 16, Scottie Barnes (22 pts, 15 reb, 8 ast) gave Toronto its first lead of the game with 2:08 left, before RJ Barrett (26 pts) added a clutch lead-extending layup in the final minute as the Raptors chased down the Clippers for a late W. |
Recap
Kings 115, Mavericks 100:
After back-to-back 30-balls, rookie Darius Acuff Jr. stayed hot for Sacramento with 25 points and 6 dimes, as the Kings used a 61-47 2nd half to outlast Cooper Flagg (17 pts, 6 ast) and the Mavs for their first win of the season. |
Recap
5. U.S. ELECTION DAY IS HERE: MAKE YOUR VOICE HEARD
Michael Starghill Jr./NBAE via Getty Images
After all 30 teams
took the court Monday, the NBA pauses play today for Election Day, encouraging Americans to make their voices heard at the ballot box.
As
NBA.com’s Ben Lambert details
,
the league’s 2026
Get In The Game. VOTE
campaign brings together players, coaches and teams to promote civic participation, with efforts spanning social media, community outreach and more. |
NBA Election Day Hub
Getting Involved:
Thunder guard Jared McCain created a
public service announcement for the campaign
, lending his skills as a TikTok creator to the initiative
Team Effort:
Pistons head coach JB Bickerstaff joined Duncan Robinson and Taurean Prince for a “
Teammate Talk
” about the importance of voting and making an impact in the community
Basketball returns Wednesday.
Today is about making your voice heard.

 	Pels Flock: Zion led all players with 9 points in the extra frame, while Karlo Matković (career-high 25 pts) and Derik Queen (20 pts, 7 reb, 5 ast) each finished with 20+
 	Ode To Jerome: Jerome recorded just one 30-point game in his first seven NBA seasons. He's already done it three times in six games this year


As Memphis went down for the first time, the Rockets kept rising.
Rockets 109, Celtics 93: Houston entered the night as the only team with eight players averaging double figures and leaned on that balance to hand Boston its first loss since its season opener, with eight Rockets scoring 8+ points.
Alperen Sengun (26 pts, 7 reb, 10 ast) led the way, while Marcus Smart starred defensively against his former team, helping the Rockets hold the C’s under 100 points for the first time this season. | Recap


 	New No. 1: With the win, Houston (7-1) leapfrogged Memphis for 1st place in the West, with both teams tied for the NBA's best plus-minus (+12.9)


As the Rockets ascended, Luka Dončić continued to reach new heights.
Lakers 138, Heat 117: Less than 24 hours after posting an unprecedented stat line, Luka rewrote more records, racking up 42 points, 13 dimes, 7 boards and 6 treys as the Lakers sprinted past Giannis Antetokounmpo (30 pts, 12 reb, 7 ast) and Miami for their second win in two nights. | Recap


 	Historic Heater: It’s Dončić’s fifth straight game with 35+ pts, 5+ reb, 5+ ast and 5+ 3s, matching Damian Lillard (Jan. 2020) for the longest such streak in NBA history
 	Absurd Averages: Over those five games, Luka is averaging a ridiculous 43.4 pts, 8.6 ast, 8.4 reb and 6.8 3s per game, capped by 40-pieces on back-to-back nights
 	Generational Problem: To top it off? Monday marked his 19th career game with 40+ points, 10+ dimes and 5+ triples, passing James Harden (18) for the most all-time




2. MORE WEST WINS: SGA & STEPH TAKE OVER, SPURS & BLAZERS STAY HOT

Two more former scoring champions took over Monday with timely outbursts.
Thunder 117, Cavaliers 112: In a game that featured an NBA season-high 23 lead changes, the reigning Kia Clutch Player of the Year – and back-to-back Kia MVP – delivered the decisive swing, as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (43 pts, 8 ast) buried a tiebreaking 3 with 33 ticks left to lift OKC over Cleveland. | Recap


 	Taking Charge: SGA scored 26 points in the 2nd half, 13 in each quarter, while matching his career-high with 35 FGA to help snap the shorthanded Thunder's two-game skid
 	“There’s certain nights, when you have a player like that, when you just kind of unleash them,” said Thunder coach Mark Daigneault of SGA postgame. “And he had it going.”



Warriors 116, Suns 113: Back from a one-game absence, Steph Curry picked up right where he left off (34 pts, 6 reb, 7 ast), erupting for an 18-point 3rd quarter as Golden State rallied past Devin Booker (26 pts, 5 ast) and Phoenix for its fifth straight dub. | Recap

 	3rd-Quarter Blitz: With the Warriors down six at the half, Curry turned up, going 4-for-5 from deep to spark a 42-point barrage from Golden State, which held off a late Phoenix push to move to 5-3
 	30 For 30: Curry has dropped 30+ points in three straight games (44, 31, 34), climbing to 2nd in the NBA in scoring (30 ppg)
 	More Dubs: After a monster Sunday, Yaxel Lendeborg tallied 16 points and 5 dimes, while Brandin Podziemski scored 20


Also winners of five straight? The reigning West champs.
Spurs 119, Jazz 97: Seven Spurs reached double figures, powered by their young backcourt tandem of Dylan Harper (17 pts, 7 reb, 8 ast) and Stephon Castle (16 pts, 4 ast), as San Antonio rolled past Utah to move to 5-2 after an 0-2 start. | Recap


 	Wemby’s Way: Victor Wembanyama, the Western Conference Player of the Week for Week 2, added 12 points, 11 boards, 5 dimes and 3 blocks in the win

Blazers 118, Nuggets 110: Jamal Murray (35 pts, 6 ast) and Nikola Jokić (26 pts, 9 reb, 8 ast, 4 stl) put on a show in Mile High, but the Blazers came out on top, climbing out of a 14-point 1st-half hole to edge Denver. | Recap

 	Blazing Hot: Deni Avdija (28 pts, 5 ast) and Damian Lillard (20 pts, 6 ast) powered Portland’s attack, which ranks 4th in scoring (120.2 ppg)
 	Two-Way Trouble: Donovan Clingan (17 pts, 18 reb, 4 blk) and Jrue Holiday (17 pts, 10 ast) delivered on both ends, helping hold Denver to 38.5% from the field after halftime
 	On The Up: Portland is now 5-1, sitting just a game back of Houston for 1st place in the West




3. EAST HEAT: SIXERS SHINE, PISTONS ROLL, KNICKS RESPOND


76ers 126, Bulls 107: Tyrese Maxey (26 pts, 11 ast), Jaylen Brown (25 pts, 11 reb) and VJ Edgecombe (21 pts) all scored 20+, with Maxey dropping 15 in the 4th as the Sixers pulled past Chicago for their fourth straight win, improving to an East-best 7-1. | Recap

 	Philly Five: LeBron James (7 reb, 9 ast) and Joel Embiid (8 reb) added 15 points apiece as the Sixers’ starting five combined for 102
 	Ty Time: Maxey, who ranks 3rd in the NBA in scoring (29.1 ppg), leads the league with 88 4th-quarter points – 26 more than the next closest player (Ty Jerome: 62)
 	Rookie Shine: No. 4 overall pick Caleb Wilson paced Chicago with a big all-around night (24 pts, 7 reb, 4 ast, 4 stl)



Pistons 124, Hornets 91: Detroit’s top-rated defense held Charlotte to just 38.1% from the field, while Cade Cunningham took over on both ends (33 pts, 5 reb, 7 ast, 5 stl) as the Pistons secured their third straight dub to move to 6-1. | Recap

 	DBo From Deep: Duncan Robinson added 24 points on 6-for-9 shooting from 3. He now has four games with 5+ triples this season, trailing only Luka (6)

Knicks 103, Nets 90: Down four after three quarters, the Knicks opened the 4th on a 25-5 run to take control, racing past the rival Nets to earn a timely win. Landry Shamet led the way with 22 points on four 3s, while Karl-Anthony Towns added a double-double (11 pts, 16 reb). | Recap



4. ROUNDUP: DYBANTSA, NAW & BALL SHOW OUT, RAPTORS & KINGS WIN


Wizards 103, Magic 94: The high-flying connection between AJ Dybantsa (21 pts, 5 reb) and Trae Young continues to grow, while Anthony Davis continues to eat (27 pts, 9 reb, 4 stl) as the Wiz earned their second straight win to move to 4-3. | Recap

 	New Era, Strong Start: Young tallied 15 points and 9 dimes, helping Washington move above .500 through seven games for the first time in five years

Hawks 108, Pacers 104: A six-man Pacers rotation gave the Hawks everything they could handle, but there was no cooling down Nickeil Alexander-Walker, who drilled nine 3s en route to a game-high 34 points as Atlanta held off Indy. | Recap



Wolves 112, Bucks 100: LaMelo Ball (34 pts, 6 3s) netted 24 points in the 1st half on five treys, before Minnesota used a 16-5 run to take control early in the 4th, riding another strong defensive effort for its fifth win in eight games. | Recap

 	Minny Clamps: The Wolves, who rank 2nd in defensive rating (104.6), have held their opponents to 106 points or fewer in all five of their wins

Raptors 125, Clippers 118: Down as many as 16, Scottie Barnes (22 pts, 15 reb, 8 ast) gave Toronto its first lead of the game with 2:08 left, before RJ Barrett (26 pts) added a clutch lead-extending layup in the final minute as the Raptors chased down the Clippers for a late W. | Recap
Kings 115, Mavericks 100: After back-to-back 30-balls, rookie Darius Acuff Jr. stayed hot for Sacramento with 25 points and 6 dimes, as the Kings used a 61-47 2nd half to outlast Cooper Flagg (17 pts, 6 ast) and the Mavs for their first win of the season. | Recap





5. U.S. ELECTION DAY IS HERE: MAKE YOUR VOICE HEARD


After all 30 teams took the court Monday, the NBA pauses play today for Election Day, encouraging Americans to make their voices heard at the ballot box.
As NBA.com's Ben Lambert details, the league's 2026 Get In The Game. VOTE campaign brings together players, coaches and teams to promote civic participation, with efforts spanning social media, community outreach and more. | NBA Election Day Hub


 	Getting Involved: Thunder guard Jared McCain created a public service announcement for the campaign, lending his skills as a TikTok creator to the initiative
 	Team Effort: Pistons head coach JB Bickerstaff joined Duncan Robinson and Taurean Prince for a “Teammate Talk” about the importance of voting and making an impact in the community

Basketball returns Wednesday. Today is about making your voice heard.

- 来源：NBA.com《Starting 5: Monday's packed 15-game slate ahead of Election Day》，发布时间 2026-11-03 15:44（美东时间，即北京时间 11-04 04:44）。链接：https://www.nba.com/news/starting-5-november-3-2026

## 2. 伤病：步行者 11 人伤停，仅 6 人应战老鹰
- 步行者对老鹰一战有 11 名球员因伤/轮休缺阵（约占球队薪资 93%），只能派出 6 人轮换，最终 104-108 落败。
- 缺阵名单包括：哈利伯顿（腿筋）、西亚卡姆（轮休）、内姆哈德（颈部）、内史密斯（腿筋）、托平（腰椎扭伤）、祖巴茨（脚踝）、麦康奈尔（腿筋）、奥孔武？——原文为 Johnny Furphy（膝）、T.J. McConnell（腿筋）、Larry Nance Jr.（生病）、Ben Sheppard（膝）；凯利·乌布雷赛前因膝部挫伤临时退出。
- 主帅卡莱尔赛前称这是“各种情况同时发生的完美风暴”，并表示“必须聪明应对”。
- 来源：NBA.com 转载美联社《5 starters, 1 sub: Pacers down to 6 players vs. Hawks》，发布时间 2026-11-03 04:18（美东时间，即北京时间 11-03 17:18）。链接：https://www.nba.com/news/5-starters-1-sub-pacers-down-to-6-players-for-game-against-atlanta-because-of-injuries-rest

（更正说明：上条缺阵名单中“奥孔武”为误写，应删除；以原文列出的球员为准。）

## 3. 伤病：莱昂纳德完成左膝消肿治疗，启动“回归比赛”流程
- 猛龙官方宣布，莱昂纳德“已成功完成针对左膝肿胀的治疗”，开始“回归比赛（return to play）”流程。
- 他将至少再缺席 3 场，球队一周后更新进展；按此推算，最早可能在 11 月 11 日对阵凯尔特人时复出。
- 莱昂纳德本季前两场场均 19.5 分 7.5 篮板，缺阵期间猛龙 2 胜 3 负。
- 来源：NBA.com 转载美联社《Raptors say Leonard has started 'return to play' process》，发布时间 2026-11-04 01:17（美东时间，即北京时间 11-04 14:17）。链接：https://www.nba.com/news/kawhi-leonards-knee-swelling-has-been-treated-and-hell-start-return-to-play-process-raptors-say
